Northern Triangle Deep Dive Follow-Up
Meta looks forward to continuing this conversation and our collaboration. Please see further information
on the topics we discussed below.
Points of Contact
The main points of contact to follow up on any issue in Central America for the Missions in El Salvador,
Guatemala and Honduras are
iñigo Fernández
[contact omitted]) and Deborah Galindo
[contact omitted]), from our local team. The main points of contact for the US team in
Washington are Brian Rice
[contact omitted]) and Sandy Luff
[contact omitted]).
Next Steps
We're happy to provide you and your team with specific training on:
• Our Community Standards.
•
Best practices on our platforms so that you and your team can take advantage of all the tools
available.
• Any of the programs we will deploy as part of our commitment to the Partnership for Central
America.
If you wish to go into greater detail in any of the topics below, we can set up a call for the specific issue.
Thank you.
Activities in Central America
As mentioned, we have an increasing commitment to the development of Central America and a greater
role in the Partnership for Central America. Below, we'd like to share additional information on the
programs we will deploy. These aim to support entrepreneurs and small business owners; and empower
youth to thrive in the digital era.
Programs to support entrepreneurs and small business owners
Over the next three years we will deliver the following programs to provide free digital skills training to
entrepreneurs and small business owners in Central America, enabling them to harness our apps to
connect with their customers:
• MetaBoost: a free comprehensive training program aimed at entrepreneurs and small business
owners in order to build and drive their digital skills to support their economic growth. The
program can be delivered in a hybrid model, online and through in-person training sessions. The
site is available in an array of languages, and you will automatically see it in the language you
have set up.
• #SheMeansBusiness (site in Spanish): our long-term commitment to women's economic
empowerment. This program supports women-owned enterprises to enter the digital economy
through skills training and business inspiration. In 2020, we expanded its scope and added
training on business resiliency through financial education. The training resources for this

program are free and can be accessed in English and Spanish and several other languages all
around the world.
Programs to empower youth to thrive in the digital era
With the following programs, young people will be able to acquire a variety of skills, including digital
literacy, digital marketing, and the use of XR technologies, that will help them harness the opportunity of
the digital revolution:
• We Think Digital (site in Spanish): this program provides resources to build a global community
of responsible digital citizens equipped with the necessary skills to thrive in a digital world. It was
developed in collaboration with experts, academics, non-governmental organizations (NGOs),
and civil society organizations across the globe. Our resources are designed to foster responsible
citizenship and are available in both English and Spanish.
• Meta Blueprint: our learning platform with hundreds of fast, free, self-guided online courses to
help businesses build their marketing skills and take advantage of the tools available to them
across our platforms.
Elections and Integrity Efforts
We are committed to protecting Election Integrity all over the world. Over the last few years, we have
made significant investments in teams and technologies to better protect elections, provide
transparency, empower people to vote, and create safe technologies. To achieve this, we have taken
significant steps to prevent election interference, fight misinformation and increase transparency:
• Our security teams investigate and take down coordinated networks of inauthentic accounts,
Pages and Groups that seek to manipulate public debate. This year, we shared our pilot guarterly
adversarial threat report that provides a broad view into the risks we see worldwide and across
multiple policy violations (see version in Spanish here). Our next quarterly threat report will be
published August 4.
• In October 2021, a month before the elections in Nicaragua, we removed a network of
896 Facebook accounts, 132 Pages, 24 Groups and 362 Instagram accounts in Nicaragua.
This operation targeted domestic audiences in that country and was linked to the
government of Nicaragua and the Sandinista National Liberation Front (FSLN) party. We
found one portion of this network through our internal investigation into suspected
coordinated inauthentic behavior in the region, and another portion - as a result of
reviewing public reporting about some of this activity. More information in our October
2021 Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior Report.
Also in 2021, we removed 12 Facebook accounts, 172 Pages and 11 accounts on
Instagram of a network that originated primarily in Mexico and targeted audiences in
Honduras, Ecuador, El Salvador, the Dominican Republic and Mexico. We found this
activity as a result of reviewing public reporting about some of this activity. More
information in our December 2021 Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior Report.

• This year, we removed 233 Facebook accounts, 84 Pages, two Groups, and 27 Instagram
accounts for violating our policy against coordinated inauthentic behavior. This network
originated in Costa Rica and El Salvador and targeted primarily Costa Rica and El
Salvador. We found this network after reviewing public reporting about an off-platform
portion of this activity and took action ahead of the election in Costa Rica.
• We work closely with civil society organizations that are critical partners in helping us better
understand the impact of our platforms and the context of the diverse communities in which we
operate around the globe. We've built the Trusted Partner program to foster this partnership
with civil society, strengthen the social media monitoring capacity of local organizations and
improve our policies, enforcement processes, and products to help keep users safe on our
platforms.
• Through our Third-Party Fact-Checking Program we help prevent the spread of misinformation
and provide additional context so people can make informed decisions. We work with
independent, third-party fact-checking organizations who are certified through the non-partisan
International Fact-Checking Network (IFCN) to identify, review and take action on this content. A
map of our fact-checking partners can be found here.
• We provide an industry-leading level of transparency around political advertising and pages. Our
Ads Transparency Tools are available globally for advertisers who want to place ads about social
issues, elections or politics thanks to which these now require authorization and include "Paid
for by" disclaimers. Recently, we announced the expansion of these tools to 19 additional
countries in Latin America.
• We maintain a dedicated team to prevent abuse in WhatsApp focused on three lines of effort:
maintaining the private nature of WhatsApp, preventing coordinated misuse of WhatsApp, and
empowering users to counteract misinformation. The detailed actions we have taken regarding
WhatsApp can be found here.
• We build strategic partnerships around the region to support the integrity of electoral processes.
For example:
• We signed a Cooperation Agreement with the Organization of American States to
continue improving responses to issues such as disinformation, electoral integrity,
freedom of expression and the protection of human rights defenders, in pursuit of
having an increasingly plural online and offline debate.
This year, we partnered with the Electoral Authority of Costa Rica (TSE) and the local
chapter of the United Nations to launched a safety guide to counter political violence
against women. Likewise, in 2021 in Mexico, we partnered with the Electoral Authority
(INE) and the local chapter of the United Nations to launch #SheLeads, a guide that
includes safety tools and best practices for building communities on Facebook, as well as
steps to take to report harassment; and an Instagram Safety Guide for Women in Politics.
Towards the upcoming elections in Brazil, we are working with the Electoral Authority to
protect the democratic process, identify and act on threats and help people gain access
to reliable information about the vote. As part of this work, we will be directing people
using Facebook and Instagram in Brazil to official information about the voting system
and articles countering misinformation about the electoral process.

Finally, our Community Standards aim to find the right balance between giving people a place to express
themselves and promoting a welcoming and safe environment for everyone. In our Transparency Center
we detail the actions taken to create our policies, remove problematic content, reduce its distribution
and inform people. A comprehensive explanation of our Community Standards can be found in this post.
We have alsomade numerous efforts to give people control over what they share, who they share it
with, the content they see and experience, and who can contact them. In our Safety Center you may find
additional information on these actions as well as resources.
Recently, we launched our First Annual Human Rights Report on how we're addressing our human rights
impacts, including insights and actions from our human rights due diligence on products, countries and
responses to emerging crises. As well as our work protecting the privacy of journalists and human rights
defenders, increasing youth safety on Instagram, fighting exploitation across our apps and protecting
free and fair elections around the world.
Again, if you wish to go into greater detail in any of the topics below, we would be happy to set up a call
for the specific issue. Thank you.
